prerequisites: Linear Algebra: vector and matrix calculus.
Calculus and Advanced Calculus: operations with derivatives, integrals and solving differential equations.
Mechanics and Thermodynamics: fundamentals of kinematics, dynamics and energy transfer.
Strength of Materials: basic concepts of stress and strain.

learning_outcomes.text: Understand and mathematically express the physical principles of Fluid Mechanics.
Apply the principles of Fluid Mechanics to solve problems in the field of Engineering, evaluating and adopting reasonable simplifications in each situation.
Interpret the variables of the fluid field and analyze the state of fluid dynamic processes from their values.
Calculate, design and interpret the operation of fluid flow systems, particularly pipe and channel transport systems.
Design, create physical and numerical models, and analyze fluid flow systems.
Master the basic concepts of fluid properties and the most important variables to consider in this scientific discipline.
Master the definition and field of application of Rheology. Application of this field to flow at low Reynolds numbers.
Master the classic analysis techniques in Fluid Mechanics, i.e., differential analysis, integral analysis, and dimensional analysis.
Master the basic concepts of fluid statics applied to engineering problems.
Master concepts related to the flow of liquids and gases and their differences.
Master knowledge of applied hydrodynamics and aerodynamics.
Master methodologies for analysis and experimentation in Fluid Mechanics.

syllabus_topics: Conservation equations: differential and integral formulation
Introduction to fluid machinery and drive systems
assessment_rules: To pass the course in the ordinary call, a minimum score of 3.5 out of 10 is required on the final exam. If the final exam score is below 3.5 points, the final grade, after weighting all activities, will be limited to a maximum of 3.5 points. The final grade is calculated as 0.75 * EF + 0.05 * AP + 0.10 * EP + 0.10 * C. For the extraordinary call, if no complementary activities were completed, the final exam will be the only assessment and will be weighted at 75%, requiring a minimum score of 6.7 out of 10 to pass.
